FULL TEXT:
National Law University and Judicial
Academy, Assam
Call for Applications for advocates practicing in Mizoram
Applications are invited from eligible early-career advocates in Mizoram for the
forthcoming cohort of the Lawyer Fellowship Programme — a one-year, field-
embedded fellowship offered by the National Law University and Judicial
Academy (NLUJA), Assam, in collaboration with the Azim Premji Foundation.
About the Fellowship
The Lawyer Fellowship is an intensive, field-embedded track for practitioners with
early experience who are ready to deepen their competence and step into leadership.
Over one year, Fellows handle real casework — legal aid, public interest litigation
and rights-based advocacy — under the close guidance of senior practitioners and
NLUJA faculty, while also mentoring junior lawyers and leading community
outreach.
For Fellows drawn from Mizoram, the programme places particular emphasis on
the region's distinctive legal landscape — customary legal systems, special
constitutional arrangements, and access-to-justice challenges in remote districts —
building a network of practitioners capable of addressing both local disputes and
wider rights-based concerns.
At a glance
Who Advocates with 2–5 years of continuous practice
Where Practising in Mizoram
Duration One year, field-embedded (with in-person intensives
at NLUJA, Assam)
Cohort 2 Fellows selected across the Fellowship state
Mode Blended — field placement + periodic in-person
blocks + weekly online sessions
Award Certificate of Fellowship from NLUJA, Assam, with
an end-line impact brief
Who should apply — eligibility
You are eligible to apply if you meet all of the following:
● Enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council.
● 2 to 5 years of continuous practice (minimum 2, maximum 5) as on the last
date for applications.
● Currently practising in Mizoram.
● Proven engagement in trial / lower-court litigation, legal aid, or rights-based /
community work.
● Potential to independently manage legal-aid cases and to contribute to
systemic legal reform.
● Capacity and willingness to mentor junior lawyers.
● Able to commit to the full one-year tenure, including in-person intensive
blocks at NLUJA, Assam, and placement in a designated district.
Preference will be given to applicants practising in trial and lower courts and those
with a demonstrated commitment to public-interest law and community
engagement.
What Fellows will do
● Handle end-to-end casework — legal aid matters, public interest litigation and
systemic advocacy — under senior mentorship.
● Be embedded in a designated district or block, working with the State and
District Legal Services Authorities, NGOs and community-based
organisations.
● Mentor junior advocates and CLE participants, and facilitate peer-learning
workshops and simulations.
● Lead legal-awareness initiatives and rights-based outreach, and train local
stakeholders such as paralegals and community volunteers.
● Attend periodic in-person intensives at NLUJA, Assam, and weekly online
sessions on case strategy, advanced topics and project management.
What Fellows receive
● Intensive, structured mentorship from a senior mentor (a High Court / Senior
Advocate).
● Exposure to complex casework and a cross-jurisdictional network of
practitioners across the North-East.
● A Certificate of Fellowship from NLUJA, Assam, with an end-line impact
brief; an optional letter of recommendation for those completing with
distinction.
● Advanced workshops and access to NLUJA's academic resources and legal
databases during in-person blocks.
● Stipend / financial support & accommodation for in-person blocks — to be
paid as per project guidelines.
Representation & equity
The Fellowship is committed to a fair and inclusive cohort. At least 40% of Fellows
will be women, and at least 30% will be drawn from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled
Tribes and other marginalised backgrounds. Selection also gives attention to
geographical balance across districts.
Selection process
● Submit your application through the official Email-Id (see 'How to apply').
● Application dossier: case history, a self-authored writing sample, and a
statement of purpose.
● Shortlisting on the basis of prior commitment to legal aid, rights-based
advocacy or community engagement.
● Two-stage interview — one online and one in-person — before a panel of
senior advocates, academics and representatives of the Legal Services
Authorities.
● Final selection of Fellows, with a waitlist maintained in reserve.
What to prepare
Keep the following ready before you begin — you will upload them in the portal:
● A statement of purpose (500–800 words) on why you seek the Fellowship and
what you hope to achieve.
● A self-authored writing sample (a pleading, legal opinion, article or note).
Anonymise all client-identifying details.
● A short case history of matters you have handled (anonymised).
● Your curriculum vitae, Bar enrolment certificate, law degree, a government
photo ID, and — if applicable — category / disability certificates.
● Contact details for two referees who can speak to your practice and character.
How to apply
Applications are accepted only through E-mail:

Contact
Registrar Office, National Law University and Judicial Academy, Assam, Hajo
Road, Amingaon, Guwahati – 781031, Assam.
Phone: +91-361-2738891 Email: registrar@nluassam.ac.in
Important notes
● All information and documents submitted must be true and correct;
misrepresentation will lead to disqualification.
● Client confidentiality must be maintained — anonymise all client data in
writing samples and case histories.
● The Fellowship is an equal-opportunity programme; applications from
women, persons with disabilities and candidates from marginalised
communities are especially encouraged.
Apply online
E-mail ID: registrar@nluassam.ac.in
Send all the required documents, and submit before the deadline. (03 October
2026)
